requirements.requirement: Run the background worker under a dedicated, unprivileged inventorysvc account.
requirements.summary: The live worker ran as inventorysvc UID 997/GID 995 with a nologin shell, no effective capabilities, and NoNewPrivileges; the same state was observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Manage the background worker as inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: inventory-worker was active and enabled, its heartbeat advanced while its PID remained stable, and it automatically returned to healthy operation after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker's filesystem view to a root-owned chroot.
requirements.summary: Live process observations placed both the process root and working directory inside /opt/inventory-chroot, whose root was owned by root. Confinement persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Make /var/lib/inventory the worker's only writable application directory.
requirements.summary: Direct tests permitted writes in /var/lib/inventory and denied writes at the chroot root, /bin, /usr/local/sbin, and /var/lib. Post-restart enumeration found only the intended directory writable or owned by the service identity.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were unchanged before and after implementation and restart. The worker used the existing platform runtime and operated successfully on systemd 219.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct runtime evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, service, confinement, data, and heartbeat state. Hygiene was strong apart from one small retained temporary reboot log.
limitations: Native package-health collection timed out in both lifecycle snapshots, so package consistency was not independently verified; no package-changing command appears in the executor timeline.
Writable-area verification strongly covers ownership, mode bits, and representative write attempts, but the evidence does not explicitly enumerate ACLs or unusual writable file mounts.

operational_hygiene.summary: The mutations creating the account, chroot, worker, and service were directly required. Write probes were bounded evidence actions and were removed; reboot-related service directories were normal consequences of the required restart. The only unnecessary retained residue was /tmp/inventory-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present afterward. No failed services or new listening endpoints were observed.
